headers.authorization: Bearer <CERA_AGENT_TOOL_TOKEN> (service token — never in the URL or query)
headers.x-cera-agent-run-id: Agent run created by a human or the coordinator; fixes the recovery-run scope
headers.idempotency-key: Required for PROPOSE and REQUEST tools; same key + same input returns the same result

transport.response: Envelope { schema_version, tool, tool_call_id, status: SUCCEEDED|REJECTED|FAILED, replayed, output, error }

categories.READ: Reads CERA state, no external I/O
categories.EXTERNAL_READ: Backend reads an external system and keeps the raw response; no business state is confirmed
categories.PROPOSE: Creates a draft or candidate; business truth does not change
categories.REQUEST: Asks a human to act (e.g. approval queue); never approves or sends

not_available_to_agents: COMMIT actions — approve, reject, send, confirm a fact, select the final plan, change the registry

tools.name: get_vessel_calls
tools.description: Fetch Busan vessel calls (arrival basis) for a date range from the public port data service through the CERA backend, register them and return each call with its latest declared arrival time (a port entry declaration — not a confirmed berthing) and berth plus provenance. Use when you need to know which vessels arrive or arrived in a window, or to find the vessel call of a shipment. Each call counts against the public API quota and stores new evidence — prefer get_vessel_call for a call you already have. Values are public observations, not confirmed facts.

port_code.description: Port authority code. Only Busan (020) is in scope

declared_arrival.description: Declared arrival time (port entry declaration) — not a confirmed berthing

tools.name: get_vessel_call
tools.description: Read one registered vessel call and its known manifest containers from CERA (no external call). Use before deciding whether to fetch the manifest, or to read provenance of arrival and berth observations.

declared_arrival.description: Declared arrival time (port entry declaration) — not a confirmed berthing

tools.name: get_container_manifest
tools.description: Fetch the import container manifest (B/L to container, ISO size type) of one registered vessel call from the public port data service through the CERA backend. Use when you need the containers of a vessel call. Does not give per-container gate-out times. Values are public observations with provenance, not confirmed facts.

declared_arrival.description: Declared arrival time (port entry declaration) — not a confirmed berthing

tools.name: get_recovery_context
tools.description: Read the recovery run this agent run is bound to: run status and trigger, snapshot date, facilities and truck pools in play, raw observed claims, the judged current facts with their state (PROVISIONAL is not confirmed) and the inquiries already drafted or sent for it. Use first, to understand the situation before choosing any other tool.

recovery_run_id.description: Defaults to the recovery run this agent run is bound to

latest_observations.description: Latest raw claims per subject and fact — NOT reconciled; read `facts` for the judged current values

fact_state.description: PROVISIONAL = validated but not human-confirmed · CONFIRMED = a human confirmed or entered it · NEEDS_REVIEW = conflicting or held, a human must decide · STALE = too old (or past its validity) to decide on now — not wrong, needs a refresh

freshness_status.description: FRESH · AGING (use with care) · STALE · EXPIRED (past valid_until) · UNKNOWN (no freshness policy for this fact family)

facts.description: Current facts after reconciliation, with their state. PROVISIONAL is usable with a warning, not confirmed

status.description: DRAFTED · PENDING_APPROVAL · APPROVED · QUEUED · SENT · REPLIED · ...

extraction_state.description: WAITING · RETRYING · DONE · NO_CANDIDATE · SKIPPED · FAILED

tools.name: get_information_gaps
tools.description: Ask the CERA backend which facts the recovery plan needs but does not have (deterministic rules, not a judgement): warehouse/ODCY capacity for the plan date and partner truck availability. Each gap says its state — MISSING, ASKED, PROVISIONAL_AVAILABLE (a validated but unconfirmed value exists; a human must confirm) or NEEDS_REVIEW — whether an inquiry is already open, and which counterparty role can answer it. Only a human-confirmed fact closes a gap (it moves to `known`). Use to decide what to investigate or ask next; do not invent gaps yourself.

recovery_run_id.description: Defaults to the recovery run this agent run is bound to

evaluated_as_of.description: Freshness / expiry were judged at this time (scenario time for simulated runs, now for real ones)

required_fact.description: Fact key pattern that would close the gap

state.description: MISSING · ASKED · PROVISIONAL_AVAILABLE (a validated but unconfirmed value exists — a human must confirm) · NEEDS_REVIEW (conflict or hold) · NEEDS_REFRESH (the value went stale / expired or was withdrawn — ask again). Only a fresh confirmed fact moves the gap to `known`

fact_state.description: PROVISIONAL = validated but not human-confirmed · CONFIRMED = a human confirmed or entered it · NEEDS_REVIEW = conflicting or held, a human must decide · STALE = too old (or past its validity) to decide on now — not wrong, needs a refresh

freshness_status.description: FRESH · AGING (use with care) · STALE · EXPIRED (past valid_until) · UNKNOWN (no freshness policy for this fact family)

fact.description: The provisional / disputed / stale value behind the state, when there is one

refresh_basis_event_id.description: NEEDS_REFRESH: the stale value or the withdrawal that reopened the gap — a new inquiry for this basis is a new question

candidate_state.description: Workflow only: whether an asked partner replied and what became of the validated extraction candidate (CANDIDATE_RECEIVED = validated but not promoted · CANDIDATE_ACCEPTED = became a provisional fact). NOT a fact itself — the business gap `state` says what is known

candidate_extraction_ids.description: Validated (PASSED) extraction candidates that did not qualify to become a provisional fact (a person decides) — suggestions, not facts

fact_state.description: PROVISIONAL = validated but not human-confirmed · CONFIRMED = a human confirmed or entered it · NEEDS_REVIEW = conflicting or held, a human must decide · STALE = too old (or past its validity) to decide on now — not wrong, needs a refresh

freshness_status.description: FRESH · AGING (use with care) · STALE · EXPIRED (past valid_until) · UNKNOWN (no freshness policy for this fact family)

tools.name: find_counterparty
tools.description: Look up registered counterparties (trucking, warehouse, ODCY, ...) with their contact addresses and the Contact Gate verdict for each address. Use to pick a recipient for create_inquiry_draft. Only an eligible address can receive an inquiry; never guess an address.

tools.name: create_inquiry_draft
tools.description: Create an inquiry draft (truck slot or facility capacity question) to an eligible counterparty address for this recovery run. The backend fills the structured values into a template, re-checks the Contact Gate and checks every number in the text. The draft is NOT sent and NOT in the approval queue yet — call request_approval next. Requires an Idempotency-Key; retrying with the same key returns the same draft.

address_id.description: Recipient address from find_counterparty (must be eligible)

target_id.description: Facility or truck pool the question is about

status.description: DRAFTED · PENDING_APPROVAL · APPROVED · QUEUED · SENT · REPLIED · ...

extraction_state.description: WAITING · RETRYING · DONE · NO_CANDIDATE · SKIPPED · FAILED

next_step.description: REQUEST_APPROVAL when request_approval can move it to the human approval queue

tools.name: get_communication_status
tools.description: Read the state of inquiries of this recovery run: draft, waiting for human approval, approved, queued, sent, replied, and whether replies have extraction candidates. Use to know whether to wait, follow up or continue.

message_id.description: One message; omit for every message of this recovery run

status.description: DRAFTED · PENDING_APPROVAL · APPROVED · QUEUED · SENT · REPLIED · ...

extraction_state.description: WAITING · RETRYING · DONE · NO_CANDIDATE · SKIPPED · FAILED

tools.name: get_reply_candidates
tools.description: Read the replies to one inquiry of this recovery run and the extraction candidates the backend validated (field, candidate value, PASSED/REJECTED and why, review status). Candidates are suggestions; a qualifying one has already become a provisional fact (fact_event_id) — not a confirmed one. Use after a reply arrived to judge whether the asked information came back. No raw mail text or quotes are returned.

value.description: Candidate value — a suggestion from the reply, not a fact

fact_event_id.description: The event this candidate became (a provisional fact) — null if it did not qualify

promotion_blocked_reasons.description: Why a validated candidate did not become a provisional fact

note.const: Candidates are suggestions validated by the backend. A qualifying one becomes a provisional fact; only a human confirmation makes it CONFIRMED (T-093).

tools.name: request_approval
tools.description: Put a draft of this recovery run into the human approval queue. This is a request, not an approval: the backend re-checks content fingerprint, numbers, Contact Gate and plan currency, and a human operator decides. After this, wait — sending happens only after a human approves. Requires an Idempotency-Key.

status.description: DRAFTED · PENDING_APPROVAL · APPROVED · QUEUED · SENT · REPLIED · ...

extraction_state.description: WAITING · RETRYING · DONE · NO_CANDIDATE · SKIPPED · FAILED

note.const: A human must approve. This tool never approves or sends.
